summary: Initial implementation kickoff to align on activation runway, security constraints, and pilot benchmarks. Customer prefers dedicated/private deployment but needs cost scenarios and VPC design details. Immediate deliverables: pricing scenarios, security pack, and pilot test matrix.
transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-07-16
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE); Priya Reddy (Redwood CSM); Jasper Liu (Redwood SE); Marina Cole (Summerset Eng Mgr); Omar Aziz (Summerset Cloud Architect); Lena Park (Summerset Security)

Summary: quick kick off to align ops, security, and pilot. Capture next steps for pricing and pilot setup.

[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. We'll do quick intros then dive into the activation runway. Priya and Jasper will handle the onboarding timeline and technical plan.
[00:18] Marina: Hi all, thanks, excited. We want to get clear on the timeline - Q4 launch target and a pilot in late July, maybe early August.
[00:35] Priya (CSM): Great. Quick question on success criteria — are you primarily looking at latency SLOs, cost per 1k tokens, or both?
[00:50] Marina: Both, but latency for customer-facing chat is highest priority. Cost matters for scale - we're forecasting 10M tokens/month in steady state.
[01:12] Jasper (SE): Okay, latency SLOs—are you targeting p95 under 300ms? Also, do you have a preference for dedicated vs hosted? Dedicated gives more predictable latency but requires networking.
[01:33] Omar: We prefer dedicated because of data residency and egress controls; also want VPC peering to our GCP project. Security will be a showstopper if we can't do private deployments.
[01:50] Lena (Security): Yep, SOC 2 and audit logs are required. We also need SSO via SAML, role-based access, and KMS integration for key rotation.
[02:10] Alex: That's all supported—Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS, and we have audit logs. Jasper will follow up on the specific KMS providers supported. I'll also link the security pack after the call.
[02:40] Jasper: Quick note - we will need an IP allowlist and a short window for peering setup. For benchmarks, do you have a staging VPC with sample traffic patterns we can run against?
[03:05] Marina: We don't yet, but we can spin up a small staging cluster. We'll share estimated QPS and traffic bursts.
[03:22] Alex: Excellent. For the pilot, we usually do a 2-week benchmark: baseline hosted test, then dedicated run, capture p50/p95/p99, token costs, and steady-state throughput. Does that align?
[03:44] Omar: Yes. Also can you simulate prefix caching and session affinity? Our chat workloads keep long context windows.
[04:01] Jasper: We'll include a KV cache warmup and typical session lengths. We'll instrument token-level costs in the report.
[04:18] Marina: What's the expected timeline to get dedicated capacity up? We have compliance review in mid-August.
[04:30] Alex: With our standard process, dedicated can be provisioned in 10-14 business days after contract. If you need faster, there's a priority onboarding add-on.
[04:49] Lena: Pricing—can you provide reserved capacity vs pay-as-you-go scenarios? We need budget sign-off.
[05:03] Alex: Absolutely. I'll share a pricing scenarios spreadsheet with reserved commitments, burst rates, and an estimated unit cost. We'll include cost comparisons to hosted.
[05:18] Marina: Any competitors we should consider? We looked at Anthropic's enterprise offering and also evaluated Vertex managed endpoints.
[05:30] Priya: Noted. We'll highlight where Redwood's routing and caching reduce per-token cost compared to standard endpoints.
[05:48] Jasper: A couple technical clarifications: what quantization profiles do you support for the model variants, and can we pin model versions during rollout?
[06:05] Alex: Yes—model pinning and rollout policies are supported. Quantization recommendations will be part of Redwood Optimize suggestions; Jasper will run a quick compatibility check during the pilot.

--- Transcript continues with timestamped back-and-forth ---
[12:10] Marina: We have an internal requirement that any external logs be redacted of PII before leaving our VPC, is that possible?
[12:28] Jasper: By default, log forwarding can be configured to redact fields. We can also route logs to your Splunk via secure collector. We'll document the redaction patterns.
[18:05] Omar: For networking, does Redwood require dedicated peering or is NAT gateway sufficient for private deployments?
[18:22] Alex: We can support both; peering gives lower variance. For regulatory workloads, peering + private deployment is recommended.
[21:03] Lena: About KMS—we use Cloud KMS with customer-managed keys, can Redwood integrate with that or do we need HSM?
[21:18] Jasper: Cloud KMS is supported; we also support HSM integrations for extra assurance. We'll capture the exact cipher suites in the security pack.
[28:40] Marina: Ok, let's talk runbook and roles. Priya, will you own the onboarding runbook?
[28:51] Priya: Yes, I'll own runbook updates. We'll need a primary contact for network and a separate contact for security.
[29:10] Marina: Omar will own networking, Lena will own security. I'll be overall program lead.
[31:55] Jasper: For pilot metrics—what thresholds should we consider pass/fail? E.g., p95 < 400ms and cost delta under 20% versus hosted?
[32:11] Marina: p95 < 350ms would be ideal, but we can be flexible to 400ms for pilot. Cost target: < 25% higher than hosted if latency gains are evident.
[35:00] Alex: Good. We'll provide an initial proposal listing two pilot scenarios: conservative (lower capacity) and full-scale (higher capacity). The conservative plan aims for speed to results.
[39:14] Marina: Regarding SSO and user access—do you require SCIM for user provisioning or can we do manual RBAC?
[39:29] Priya: We support SCIM and manual invites. For enterprise rollouts we recommend SCIM to sync groups.
[42:40] Omar: One more item—data residency. Some tenant data must be kept in EU regions. Can you guarantee region pinning?
[42:55] Alex: Yes we have region pinning for model serving and data at rest. We'll note the available regions for Private deployments in the follow-up.
[46:10] Marina: This is helpful, thanks. Let's recap next steps.
[46:20] Priya: Recap: Alex sends pricing scenarios; Jasper schedules the pilot and shares the test matrix; Marina/Omar will provide traffic samples and provision staging VPC; Priya sends onboarding runbook and permissions checklist.
[46:40] Marina: Agreed. Also please share the security pack and SOC 2 evidence link.
[46:55] Alex: Will do. I'll drop links: security pack (https://redwood-internal.docs/security-pack.pdf), onboarding runbook (https://redwood-internal.docs/onboarding-runbook), pricing gsheet (link will be shared). We'll also create a pilot workspace in Slack.
[47:20] Omar: Expect traffic patterns by 2026-07-20. We want pilot to start week of 2026-07-27 if possible.
[47:40] Jasper: We'll aim to have the benchmark plan by 2026-07-24 and the pilot runbook by 2026-07-26.
[48:05] Lena: I'll follow up with any compliance questions; otherwise we can proceed.
[48:30] Alex: Great thanks — we'll follow up via email and Slack and set the pilot kickoff calendar invite. Thanks everyone.
[48:45] Meeting ends.

Questions captured:
- Do you need HSM or Cloud KMS? (answered)
- Can you do VPC peering or NAT? (answered)

Action items noted above.
